title: TPvG: A Moral Decision Framework for Large Language Models from One-Shot to Sequential Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2608.28610v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing LLM moral evaluations typically present models with isolated moral vignettes and elicit a single-shot decision, neglecting a factor known to profoundly influence human moral behavior: consequence feedback. We introduce TPvG (Text-based Pain-versus-Gain), adapted from a human moral paradigm, which embeds consequence feedback into an everyday moral dilemma of not harming others versus maximising self-gain. TPvG comprises five moral decision tasks, progressing from minimal-context one-shot choices to sequential decisions with explicit consequence feedback. Our results show that LLM moral decisions were strongly affected by decision format (one-shot versus sequential), and explicit receiver feedback produced heterogeneous effects across models. translated_title: TPvG：从单次决策到序列反馈的大语言模型道德决策框架
translated_abstract: 现有的LLM道德评估通常向模型呈现孤立的道德情境并引出单次决策，忽略了一个已知会深刻影响人类道德行为的因素：后果反馈。我们提出了TPvG（基于文本的痛苦与收益权衡）框架，该框架改编自人类道德研究范式，将后果反馈嵌入到一个日常道德困境中，即在“不伤害他人”与“最大化自身收益”之间进行权衡。TPvG包含五个道德决策任务，从最少上下文的单次选择逐步过渡到带有明确后果反馈的序列决策。我们的结果表明，LLM的道德决策受到决策形式（单次还是序列）的强烈影响，且明确的接收者反馈在不同模型中产生了异质性的效应。此外，LLM对明确接收者反馈的反应与人类参考模式存在分歧，表明其决策过程可能有所不同。这些发现强调了在道德评估中纳入后果反馈的必要性。
tldr: 该论文提出TPvG道德决策框架，首次将后果反馈引入大语言模型道德评估，发现决策形式与反馈显著影响模型道德决策，且其反应模式与人类存在系统性差异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TPvG, a moral decision framework that embeds consequence feedback into LLM moral evaluations, revealing that decision format and explicit feedback strongly shape model moral decisions, which diverge from human reference patterns.
